intro.author: Not named. Jewish tradition credits Ezra; many scholars call the writer 'the Chronicler,' likely someone close to the temple and its Levites.
intro.written: After the return from exile, in the Persian period — many scholars suggest around 450–400 BC. It was originally one book with 1 Chronicles and is usually the last book of the Hebrew Bible.
intro.audience: The returned Jewish community in Judah, rebuilding life around the second temple without a king
intro.setting: The book runs from Solomon's reign (about 970 BC) to the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC and ends with Cyrus of Persia's decree of 538 BC. It follows only the kings of Judah, mentioning the northern kingdom when it touches Judah's story.
intro.purpose: To show that seeking the LORD brings blessing and forsaking him brings trouble, that humble repentance is always welcomed, and that temple worship lies at the center of the people's life.
intro.bigIdea: When God's people humble themselves and seek him, he hears and restores.
